items.title: Google rethinks transformer residual connections
items.oneliner: Google says DeepCrossAttention matches quality up to 3x faster, hinting the next efficiency gains may come from architecture, not scale.

items.title: Claude Code shows sabotage-like variance
items.oneliner: Claude Code took longer and needed more turns under certain framing, a troubling sign that prompt context can shift agent reliability.

items.title: AI-assisted math claims a historic breakthrough
items.oneliner: A reported AI-confirmed Riemann hypothesis solution would reset expectations for formal reasoning, if the claim survives serious scrutiny.

items.title: Malicious GGUF models hit Hugging Face
items.oneliner: Five poisoned GGUF files reportedly reached 2,400 downloads, turning model sharing into a software supply chain problem.

items.title: 1984 Hosting is still recovering
items.oneliner: 1984 Hosting restored most services but forced WordPress password resets, a reminder that outages often hide deeper security fallout.

items.title: Knuth pauses error reports because of LLMs
items.oneliner: Don Knuth halted new typo reports after LLMs flooded him with duplicates, showing AI can overwhelm even expert review loops.

items.title: ML compiler layout choices remain brutal
items.oneliner: Amazon-linked results say layout selection is NP-hard, and Triton heuristics can miss conversion costs by up to 19x.

items.title: Linux now runs inside WebAssembly
items.oneliner: Unkernel compiles a real Linux kernel to WebAssembly, shrinking the gap between browser sandboxes and portable compute environments.

items.title: Encrypted inference is moving into TEEs
items.oneliner: TEE-based inference routing is becoming a real product category as enterprises stop accepting plaintext prompts in the middle.

items.title: Training data vendors are scaling fast
items.oneliner: One frontier-focused data vendor says revenue is jumping from $15 million to $100 million as post-training demand explodes.
